subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class delegate-only/self-deny tool policy for agents, and which API shape should own that security boundary?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but this adds public config surface and changes how tool-deny boundaries flow from requester agents to subagents, which automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Approve delegate-only config
options.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that hides selected tools from the requester model while preserving deny-wins semantics and controlled child inheritance.

options.title: Fold into per-spawn policy
options.body: Let per-spawn toolsAllow-style work own child narrowing and document that parent direct-use prevention still needs separate profiles or instructions.

options.title: Keep monotonic policy only
options.body: Reject parent-deny delegation and document the security rationale plus the separate-agent workaround.

recommendation.title: Approve delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that hides selected tools from the requester model while preserving deny-wins semantics and controlled child inheritance.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a public security-boundary/product contract decision, and the live issue timeline shows recent direct attention from steipete.
